turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I need to pick hiking boots before my trip, and I've tried on a few pairs.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hear me out on all the options before you comment.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The first pair is heavy leather boots, super sturdy and waterproof, but they need breaking in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The second pair is lightweight trail runners, really comfortable right away, but not waterproof.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the third pair is mid height synthetic boots, kind of in between, with decent ankle support.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's it. Now you can comment.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For most trips, the mid height synthetic boots are a solid compromise between comfort and support. The leather boots are best for rough, wet terrain if you have time to break them in. The trail runners are great on dry, well kept trails.
